claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 5 years old and lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 5 years old and lives with you at home.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? By this I mean, do you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and general upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I provide everything he needs like his food, clothes, and all his general care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very helpful. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living with someone else for any period of time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of that applies. Alex lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, no one else is claiming it at the moment, but there is a bit of a situation. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for him, and we can't actually agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. We've been going back and forth about it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation. That's an important detail.

To clarify: **Are you and Alex's other parent living together, or do you live separately? And does Alex live with you, with the other parent, or does he spend time at both homes?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We live separately. Alex lives with me full-time - he's here at my home all the time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just to make sure I have the complete picture:

**Does Alex's other parent contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (such as maintenance payments, or paying for clothes, food, pocket money, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not receiving any regular maintenance payments or financial contributions from Alex's other parent at the moment, no.

## Assessment Complete

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Summary

Based on the information you've provided:

- **Alex is 5 years old** (under 16) ✓
- **You live in the UK** ✓
- **Alex lives with you full-time** ✓
- **You are responsible for Alex's care and upkeep** (food, clothes, general care) ✓
- **No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex** ✓
- **Alex is not in hospital, care, or living elsewhere** ✓

### About the disagreement with Alex's other parent

You mentioned that you and Alex's other parent can't agree on who should claim. This doesn't prevent you from being eligible. According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. If two people are responsible for the same child and cannot agree between themselves who will claim, HMRC will decide who gets it.

Since Alex lives with you full-time and you're fully responsible for his care, and the other parent isn't providing financial contributions, you have a strong case for claiming.

### Next steps

You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If Alex's other parent also tries to claim, HMRC will make the decision about who should receive it based on the circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
